diagnostic_evidence.quote: By the Burkholder--Gundy--Davis inequality \cite[Theorem 3.28]{Karatzas1991-xr}, for a constant $c$, \[ \mean{\abs{\int_0^T u_{1,t}^{\epsilon-1}\,dW^{1,1}_t}^q} \le c\, \pp{\int_0^T \mean{u_{1,t}^{2\epsilon-2}}\,dt}^{q/2}. \]
The integrand on the right-hand side is bounded for $\epsilon>0$ by part 1 with $r=2-2\epsilon<2$.

issues.failure_explanation: The BGD inequality gives E[|∫u^{ε-1}dW|^q] ≤ c_q E[(∫u^{2ε-2}dt)^{q/2}], not c(∫E[u^{2ε-2}]dt)^{q/2}. For q > 2 the function x^{q/2} is convex so Jensen's inequality goes the opposite direction: E[(∫f dt)^{q/2}] ≥ (∫E[f]dt)^{q/2}. Part 1 only yields E[u^{-r}] < ∞ for r < 2, bounding E[u^{2ε-2}] but not E[u^{q(ε-1)}] needed for q > 2/(1−ε). A bootstrap argument iterating Itô with reduced ε and power could plausibly close the gap but is not supplied.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either supply a bootstrap/iteration argument handling arbitrary q, or restrict the corollary (and dependent Proposition timeregbnd Part 1) to q < 2/(1−ε), noting that downstream uses require only moderate q.
issues.overall_effect: Part 2 of Corollary cor is unproved for q ≥ 2/(1−ε). Proposition timeregbnd (Part 1) inherits this gap for large q. Downstream discretization results that use only moderate moments remain supported.
issues.title: Corollary inverse-integral moment bound unproved for large q
issues.why_classification: The proof gap requires a contained nontrivial argument (a bootstrap of moment bounds) or a limited weakening of the quantifier on q. The qualitative conclusion and downstream uses at moderate q survive.

The correct correction drift from Itô's formula is div_j M = (3/2, x/(2η))^T. These differ by (1, x/(2η))^T. Consequently the SDE is not Riemannian Langevin dynamics with metric M^{-1}: the correction drift in the standard Riemannian Langevin formula does not match the actual drift of the transformed process. The Fokker–Planck equation stated in the proposition is nevertheless correct (verified independently from the Itô computation).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: standard theory (Bakry--Emery criterion, Holley--Stroock theorem) applies to the potential $\frac 12 \lambda \|\vec x \|^2+G_3(\vec x)$, as it is a bounded perturbation (given by $G$) of a convex potential (given by $\frac12\lambda\|\vec x\|^2$).

issues.failure_explanation: The invariant measure π ∝ exp(−βH) corresponds to potential V = βH = (βλ/2)‖x‖² + βG₃(x). Holley–Stroock applied to V gives LSI constant R = βλ · exp(−β(sup G − inf G)) = βλ e^{β(inf G − sup G)}, not βλ e^{inf G − sup G}. The proof applies Holley–Stroock to the un-scaled potential (½λ‖x‖² + G₃) as if it generated π, which it does not. The missing factor of β in the exponent makes the claimed rate wrong for β ≠ 1.

issues.title: Wrong entropy decay rate in bounded-G ergodicity theorem
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local correction to the exponent (adding a factor of β), but the quantitative rate necessarily changes, losing the stated bound for β ≠ 1. The qualitative geometric convergence and scope survive, leaving a recognizably comparable result.

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding E₁,ₜ + E₂ gives 2π̃_{Δt}(P_T(φ)) − π̃_{Δt}(φ) − π(φ), which is not π_{Δt}(φ) − π(φ) in general. The correct decomposition requires three terms: [π_{Δt} − π̃_{Δt}](φ) − E₁,ₜ(Δt) + E₂(T). Additionally, the proof never establishes the uniform boundedness of π̃_{Δt}/π needed to apply Theorem thm:num_conv with initial law π̃_{Δt}, leaving a hypothesis gap.

issues.title: Invalid algebraic decomposition in convergence-to-invariant proof
